shortThesis: AI civic-letter workflow exists in code; investibility waits on paid conversion and delivery proof.

thesisCurrent.label: watchlist personal/research asset
thesisCurrent.summary: CivicState can be evaluated as a narrow paid civic correspondence workflow, but it is not yet a venture-ready business.
thesisCurrent.honesty: Repo evidence supports implementation breadth; market and operating proof remain assumptions.

adoption.note: POM soul-review + wrk.dog merge constitute adoption - operator ruling 2026-06-12; see the PR's POM record

methods: Inspected implementation surfaces under apps/web, apps/api, apps/worker, and packages/shared.
Used workspace-only evidence; no network research.

staleSignals: .planning/existing-state.md says zero application code exists, but current repo has app code [evidence: repo file scan].
.planning/ROADMAP.md marks all phases complete while .planning/REQUIREMENTS.md still marks many requirements pending [evidence: .planning files].
MASTER_PLAN.md says Next.js 14 in one summary while repo/package planning says Next.js 15 [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md; .planning/PROJECT.md].

customerDefinition.primary: U.S. resident with a specific civic concern who wants researched, cited letters to officials [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].
customerDefinition.excluded: Legal claimants, lobbying firms, nonprofits/API buyers, and automated follow-up campaign users are out of v1 [evidence: .planning/REQUIREMENTS.md].

marketSizing.approach: Bottom-up validation model; no top-down TAM claimed.
marketSizing.cohortRevenue: $1,500 gross revenue at $15 AOV [assumption: 100 x $15; AOV from MASTER_PLAN.md].
marketSizing.month24Scenario: $24,000 monthly revenue from 1,200 submissions at $20 AOV [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md].
marketSizing.tamClaim: Not claimed [assumption: workspace-only mode prevents external market sizing].

revenueModel.breakEven: $340/mo and about 25 Amplify submissions per month [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md]

competition: Resistbot [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md; assumption: current claims not externally verified]
Change.org [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md; assumption: current claims not externally verified]
LegalZoom [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md; assumption: current claims not externally verified]
Manual official contact forms/email [assumption: common free substitute]
Quorum and VoterVoice [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md; assumption: current pricing/features not externally verified]
risksAntiPlan: Consumer willingness to pay may be too low versus free email/contact forms.
Official email coverage is incomplete: Congress.gov implementation leaves email blank and local lookup is stubbed [evidence: code].
.gov deliverability may fail the paid-delivery promise.
Legal/compliance review is not evidenced; product touches sensitive political and legal-adjacent speech.
Roadmap and state docs conflict, so operator should distrust completion checkboxes until staging verification.

assumptionLedger.assumption: Users will pay $5-$25 for cited civic letters [assumption: unvalidated willingness to pay].
Official targeting can cover enough federal/state/local recipients [assumption: API coverage unproven].
assumptionLedger.test: Sample 50 ZIP codes [assumption: early coverage test].

assumptionLedger.assumption: Delivery works for government inboxes [assumption: deliverability unproven].

goToMarket.firstCohort: 25-50 known early users [assumption: controlled beta size]
channels: operator network outreach [assumption: no paid acquisition evidence]
SEO only after delivery proof [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md]

mitigations: Controlled beta with explicit conversion gate.
Seeded deliverability tests before open launch.
Operator/counsel review of terms, disclosures, opt-out, and letter framing.
residualRisks: Civic/political content may trigger provider risk review.
Official contact data may decay faster than cache refresh.
AI citation pipeline may still miss nuanced legal context.

operatorQuestions: Should registry continue presenting this as a personal/research asset or allow a business pitch?
Should public identity be brooks-history or CivicState?
Who reviews legal/compliance posture before public launch?
